steps.title: Scale the recipe
steps.prompt: The recipe card makes 2 portions. You need 4 portions. How many Spaghetti · 100 g pack are needed?
steps.teach: Work out the requested total or difference, using the units in the question.
steps.example: Three groups of 2 items contain 6 items.
steps.hint: Compare your model with the quantities and units in the task.

steps.title: Inspect the kitchen stock
steps.prompt: Look inside the cupboards and fridge. Select the quantities already available.
steps.teach: Count each product separately and compare it with the quantities you need.
steps.example: Need 4 notebooks and have 1? Put 3 on the list.
steps.hint: Count the products inside each cupboard or fridge compartment.
steps.worked: Spaghetti · 100 g pack: 1; Tomatoes · tin: 0; Mince · 100 g pack: 1
steps.instruction: Tap a product to collect one. Tap a basket item to put one back.

steps.title: Make your shopping list
steps.prompt: Use the recipe card and kitchen stock. List only the missing ingredients.
steps.teach: Count each product separately and compare it with the quantities you need.
steps.example: Need 4 notebooks and have 1? Put 3 on the list.
steps.hint: Compare each basket quantity with your saved shopping list.
steps.worked: Spaghetti · 100 g pack: 3; Tomatoes · tin: 2; Mince · 100 g pack: 3
steps.instruction: Tap a product to collect one. Tap a basket item to put one back.

steps.title: Catch the bus to the supermarket
steps.prompt: Catch the bus to the supermarket. It is 09:00. Allow 10 minutes to walk after the bus. You need to arrive by 09:40. Choose the cheapest service that gets you there in time.
steps.teach: Add walking time to each arrival before comparing eligible fares.
steps.example: A bus arriving at 08:00 plus a 10-minute walk reaches the destination at 08:10.
steps.hint: Add the walking time to each bus arrival. Compare fares only for services that arrive in time.
steps.worked: The local service reaches the destination at 09:35 and costs £1.25.

steps.title: Collect from the shelves
steps.prompt: Use your saved shopping list. Tap shelf products to put the required quantities in your basket. Leave unneeded extras on the shelf.
steps.teach: Count each product separately and compare it with the quantities you need.
steps.example: Need 4 notebooks and have 1? Put 3 on the list.
steps.hint: Compare each basket quantity with your saved shopping list.
steps.worked: Spaghetti · 100 g pack: 3; Tomatoes · tin: 2; Mince · 100 g pack: 3; Chocolate bar: 0; Fizzy drink: 0
steps.instruction: Tap a product to collect one. Tap a basket item to put one back.

steps.title: Pay for shopping
steps.prompt: The bill is £8.15. Take £10.00 from your pretend purse and place it on the counter.
steps.teach: Build the payment from UK coin and note values.
steps.example: Three groups of 2 items contain 6 items.
steps.hint: £1 is 100p. You can remove the last token.

steps.title: Collect your change
steps.prompt: You paid £10.00 for a £8.15 bill. Collect the change.
steps.teach: Work out the requested total or difference, using the units in the question.
steps.example: Three groups of 2 items contain 6 items.
steps.hint: Subtract the bill from the amount paid.

steps.title: Catch the bus home
steps.prompt: Catch the bus home. It is 09:35. Allow 10 minutes to walk after the bus. You need to arrive by 10:15. Choose the cheapest service that gets you there in time.
steps.teach: Add walking time to each arrival before comparing eligible fares.
steps.example: A bus arriving at 08:00 plus a 10-minute walk reaches the destination at 08:10.
steps.hint: Add the walking time to each bus arrival. Compare fares only for services that arrive in time.
steps.worked: The local service reaches the destination at 10:10 and costs £1.25.

steps.title: Prepare Spaghetti Bolognese
steps.prompt: Open the recipe card. Arrange the preparation actions for this meal.
steps.teach: Think about which action depends on an earlier action.
steps.example: For a different task: put socks on before putting shoes on.
steps.hint: Which action can safely happen first? What needs to be ready before the next action?
steps.worked: Measure the sauce ingredients → Simmer the protein with tomatoes in the pan → Cook the spaghetti and combine with the sauce
items: Cook the spaghetti and combine with the sauce
Simmer the protein with tomatoes in the pan
steps.instruction: Tap an action, then its position. Use every action once.

steps.title: Measure the water
steps.prompt: Use the jug to measure 1 litres of water for this batch.
steps.teach: Convert the units, then position the scale marker.
steps.hint: One litre is 1,000 ml. Tap a jug scale mark, then fine-tune if needed.

steps.title: Set the recipe temperature
steps.prompt: Use the temperature supplied on the recipe card for the hob. Do not guess a real food-safety temperature.
steps.teach: Check which option meets the requirement before comparing its cost.
steps.example: A 4-seat ticket is too small for 5 people, even when cheaper.
steps.hint: Find the temperature beside the cooking method on the recipe card.

steps.title: When will the meal be ready?
steps.prompt: Start Spaghetti Bolognese at 10:10. The recipe specifies 25 minutes. Set the finishing time.
steps.teach: Add the duration to the start time. Carry 60 minutes into the next hour.
steps.hint: Compare your model with the quantities and units in the task.

steps.title: Serve and tidy
steps.prompt: The meal is ready. Put these actions in a safe and useful order.
steps.teach: Think about which action depends on an earlier action.
steps.example: For a different task: put socks on before putting shoes on.
steps.hint: Which action can safely happen first? What needs to be ready before the next action?
steps.worked: Turn off the cooking equipment → Serve the meal → Wash the used equipment
steps.instruction: Tap an action, then its position. Use every action once.
